Marquez was booked in the 44th minute after tripping Ronaldo as he attempted to surge forward, meaning the Mexican is suspended for next Tuesday's second leg at Old Trafford. Deco tested Van der Sar with a low drive, then the Dutchman easily dealt with a 20-yard effort from Xavi. Barcelona coach Frank Rijkaard took off Messi in the 62nd minute, replacing him with teenager Bojan Krkic, who scored the winner in the first leg of the quarterfinal against Schalke. Rijkaard responded by replacing Deco with Henry in the 77th minute, and the French forward forced a scrambled save by Van der Sar with a long-range shot on 83. Ferguson brought on veteran winger Ryan Giggs for Tevez soon after, then Van der Sar denied Andres Iniesta and also dived to comfortably save Henry's free-kick from 35 yards. The titanic clash, billed as a showdown between the world’s two most electrifying talents—Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi—ended without goals, but not without immense tension. United survived an agonizing third-minute penalty miss from Ronaldo and an onslaught from the Catalan giants to leave Spain with a crucial, if precarious, clean sheet ahead of next week’s return leg at Old Trafford.

### Shock at the Camp Nou: Ronaldo’s Rare Misstep

The match burst into life almost immediately in front of a atmospheric crowd of over 95,000. Just two minutes in, United won a corner that was met by Ronaldo’s towering header. The ball struck the raised arm of Barcelona defender Gabriel Milito, leaving referee Massimo Busacca with no choice but to point to the spot.

Ronaldo, who entered the match with a staggering 38 goals to his name this season, stepped up to give Sir Alex Ferguson’s side a dream start. But in a rare moment of faltering composure, the Portuguese superstar hesitated in his run-up and blasted his right-footed spot-kick high and wide into the stands, brushing the outside of the top corner. 

It was a staggering reprieve for Frank Rijkaard’s side, and one that completely altered the psychological momentum of the evening.

### Messi Sparks Barca, Van der Sar Holds Firm

Spurred on by Ronaldo’s miss, Barcelona assumed total control of midfield, dictating the tempo through Xavi Hernández and Andrés Iniesta. Crucial to their fluidity was the sensational return of Lionel Messi. Playing his first match in six weeks after recovering from a torn thigh muscle, the young Argentine looked as though he had never been away. 

Messi tortured United’s left flank, dropping deep, weaving through double-teams, and leaving Patrice Evra grasping at shadows. Yet for all of Barcelona’s aesthetic brilliance and territorial dominance—hovering over 65% possession—they struggled to breach United’s resolute defensive wall, led imperiously by Rio Ferdinand.

When Barcelona did find a way through, they met an unbeatable barrier in Edwin van der Sar. The veteran Dutch goalkeeper produced a masterclass in positioning and composure. Midway through the first half, Van der Sar brilliantly smothered a dangerous low drive from Gianluca Zambrotta. Early in the second half, he again came to United’s rescue, comfortably dealing with a fierce strike from Samuel Eto'o and tipping a long-range Xavi effort over the crossbar.

### The Tactical Chess Match: Substitutions Shape the Final Act

As the match entered its final third, both managers turned to their benches in a high-stakes tactical chess game.

Frank Rijkaard, aware that Messi’s match fitness was waning after a energetic hour, withdrew the Argentine in the 62nd minute to a standing ovation, introducing 17-year-old prodigy Bojan Krkić to add fresh legs to the attack. Fifteen minutes later, Rijkaard made a statement of intent, bringing on former Arsenal hero Thierry Henry for Zambrotta, shifting to an all-out four-man attack. Henry almost broke the deadlock immediately, bending a trademark free-kick toward the top corner, only for the sprawling Van der Sar to beat it away.

Sir Alex Ferguson, meanwhile, orchestrated a masterclass in European game-management. Recognizing that his side was being overrun in midfield and that Wayne Rooney had been worked to exhaustion in an unfamiliar wide-right role, Ferguson made his moves. 

In the 76th minute, Rooney was replaced by the pace of Nani to offer a counter-attacking outlet. Ten minutes later, Ferguson withdrew a tireless Carlos Tevez for the experienced Ryan Giggs, instructing his side to drop into a deep, impenetrable 4-5-1 block. United sacrificed any remaining attacking ambition, opting instead to kill the game's tempo and deny Barcelona space in the final third.

### Advantage United?

When the final whistle blew, it was Ferguson who looked the happier of the two managers. While United failed to secure a precious away goal—and will rue Ronaldo’s early penalty miss—they achieved what few European teams accomplish at the Camp Nou: keeping Barcelona at bay.

"We defended very well, concentrated hard, and got a result," Ferguson told reporters after the match. "It was a disciplined performance, though we could have used the ball better. Old Trafford will be a completely different game."

For Frank Rijkaard, the frustration was palpable. Barcelona played the prettier football, but without a goal to show for their dominance, they now face a daunting task in Manchester. 

The tie remains balanced on a knife-edge. But with a spot in the Moscow final on the line, the stage is set for an epochal second leg at Old Trafford next Tuesday.
